summary: Ambiguous idempotency when orchestrating chained function calls across models with session-nonce + per-request idempotency
description:
Issue summary:
Customer runs an orchestrator that sequences multiple function/tool calls across two model endpoints (a chat model + a reranker). The client library currently attaches a short-lived session-nonce header (X-Session-Nonce) at connection start and also generates per-request idempotency keys. Under retries and client reconnect, the combination appears to cause Redwood's edge deduplication to conflate different logical requests when the session-nonce is reused by the client, resulting in suppressed second-step function calls or incorrectly deduped webhook invocations.

Impact:
- Some chained transactions are partially executed (first function runs, downstream confirmation never occurs).
- Customer reports missing downstream webhooks and duplicated retry logs that suggest the platform deduped a distinct request.
- Affects live document ingestion pipeline at SentinelDocs (enterprise/dedicated), causing ingestion lag and manual replays.

Environment:
- SDKs used: python-sdk v0.9.7 (orchestrator), go-sdk v0.8.4 (webhook handler).
- Region: prod us-east with some traffic routed via eu-west failover.
- Network: TLS via customer-managed VPC (Dedicated).

Steps to reproduce (high-level):
1) Open a session and include X-Session-Nonce header for the duration of short-lived multiplexed streams.
2) Orchestrator sends request A -> model-chat that triggers tool call T1 (external webhook).
3) Orchestrator immediately sends request B -> reranker model that includes its own idempotency-key for the chain step.
4) Simulate a client-side retry/stream reconnect (HTTP/2 RST or client reconnect) and resend B with a fresh per-request idempotency-key but the same session-nonce.
5) Observe that Redwood's edge returns 200 but only the first tool call was delivered or the webhook deduplicator discards the second chained call.

Observed logs/snippets:
- Edge logs show a deduplication hit on hash computed over (session-nonce + idempotency-key) instead of per-request key alone.
- Customer webhook receipts show T1 occurred but T2 (confirmation) missing.
- SDK retry trace shows the client attempted a resend with new per-request id but reused session cookie.

Customer-provided repro artifacts:
- Minimal python orchestrator gist (attached link): https://gist.github.com/sentineldocs/cc-orch-repro
- Webhook handler logs (redacted) showing missing confirmations between 14:02-14:08 UTC.

Expected behavior:
- Edge deduplication should be scoped to the canonical idempotency footprint (per-request idempotency-key and any canonical request body) and should not conflate different logical requests only because a session-scoped nonce was present. Session-nonce should help routing/tracing, not deduplication across distinct idempotency keys.

Initial hypothesis:
- Edge/ingress code path that normalizes idempotency keys may be combining session-scoped headers into the deduplication key under some configurations (http/2 vs http/1.1 or when header compression/trimming occurs).
- Customer-managed VPC/edge sidecar might be reusing session-nonce via connection pooling leading to hash collisions in the deduper.

Suggested immediate mitigation for customer:
- As a short-term workaround, instruct orchestrator to always rotate X-Session-Nonce on reconnects and avoid tying session-nonce into idempotency computations.
- Add server-side acknowledgement to confirm each tool invocation and surface confirmed call-ids back to caller so orchestration can self-heal on missing confirmations.

Next steps required from Redwood: 
- SRE/edge to review deduplication key material hashing and confirm which headers are included under which router profiles.
- SDK team to audit any client-side behavior that signals session-nonce as part of idempotency headers.
- If confirmed, roll a config change to exclude session-scoped headers from dedupe hash and add integration test covering multiplexed streams + reconnect scenarios.
investigation_notes: 03/12: Replayed customer's repro on staging with SDK versions reported. Reproducer initially failed to show dedupe until we forced HTTP/2 connection reuse and enabled header compression. 03/13: Found router profile 'mux-default' includes 'X-Session-Nonce' in the dedupe-key list — likely historical decision to preserve per-connection semantics. Hash function concatenates header list in stable order; when client rotates per-request idempotency-key but keeps session-nonce, the composite hash can collide/match an earlier transaction if the order/normalization differs. Edge patch candidate: remove session-scoped headers from dedupe-key set and make dedupe key strictly (idempotency-key|request-body-canonical).

resolution: Pending - SRE to propose edge config change to exclude session-scoped headers from deduplication key. SDKs to add integration tests. Customer notified of workaround (rotate session-nonce on reconnect).
workaround: Rotate X-Session-Nonce on reconnect; add an explicit per-tool confirmation ACK in orchestrator to detect missing downstream steps and retry individually.
follow_up_tasks: Edge: remove X-Session-Nonce from dedupe-key in mux-default profile and run canary
SDK: add integration test covering multiplexed stream reconnect + per-request idempotency
Support: schedule follow-up call with SentinelDocs to confirm fix
